memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you give testimony in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd," - Exodus 23:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most quietly powerful commands in all of Scripture: do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. God knows how strong the pull of the majority is. When everyone around us is moving in one direction, it takes real courage to stand still, and even more to move the other way. Yet God calls His people to let truth and righteousness — not the crowd — decide where they stand.

We feel this pressure every day. The group is gossiping, and it is awkward to stay silent. The team is cutting a corner, and speaking up would make us unpopular. The culture is celebrating something we know is wrong, and going along is so much easier than standing apart. But numbers do not make wrong become right. A thousand voices approving a lie does not turn it into truth.

God's people have always been called to a holy independence, to fear God more than the crowd. Daniel stood alone. The disciples chose to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29). And Jesus Himself walked a lonely road that no crowd would follow. Following Christ sometimes means being willing to be the only one. But we are never truly alone, for God stands with those who stand for Him. Where is He asking you to break from the crowd today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where am I tempted to follow the crowd against what I know is right?
Do I fear people's opinions more than I fear God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to stand for what is right even when I stand alone. Help me fear You more than the crowd, and trust that You are always with me. Amen.
